title: The Emperor makes his grandson Yūsuf, sixteen, eldest son of the heir Ismāʿīl and second in line, admiral of the fleet, as he himself had been made at twenty-five. Yūsuf has married three wives: Amie, daughter of Mansa Tiramakhan of Mālī; Fāṭima, daughter of the late lord of Banbalūna, to tie the ṭāʾifas to the crown; and Muʾmina, of the court

data.yusuf: born 6 January 1422 at Gharnāṭa, 66/59/52, shrewd as a child, an expensive in-depth education

wives.Amie: born 1418, daughter of Mansa Tiramakhan of Mālī, Mandinka by culture and a Sunni
wives.Fāṭima: born 1419, daughter of Yūsuf ibn Ismāʿīl, lord of Banbalūna (d. 1428)
wives.Muʾmina: born 1416, daughter of Muṣliḥ al-Dīn, a Naṣrid of the court

data.reason: the admiralty had done the Emperor good in his own mind, and he imagined it would do his grandson the same (Trent)

source: Trent's screenshot and account; save of 16 January 1438

title: For the first time the realm's temper leans to the sea rather than the land, and protected harbours are being built in the newly annexed Catalan ports: Barcelona, Girona, Tarragona, Tortosa and Perpignan

landVsNaval.note: negative is land, positive is sea

data.realm: 221 towns and 3.25 million people after Catalonia's annexation; stability 24.2; treasury 1,653, no debt

title: Majrīṭ, grown rapidly beside Ṭulayṭula into one of the most important towns of the interior, is granted a city charter. The Emperor opposed it, asking why he should favour a town so far from the sea, but the two princes pressed for it

data.emperor: 'Why should I grant such favour so far from the sea? Won't the city merely wither and die?' (Trent)
data.granted: at the two princes' urging, with a major concession from the northern nobility

title: The price of Majrīṭ's charter: the umarāʾ concede the slow unravelling of their Land Rights in the integrated territories. In return they are granted a stipend for their arts and culture, in truth a fund to keep them from open mutiny as the two princes carry on their grandfather's reform

data.privilege: Land Rights (nobles): +5% satisfaction and +75% power for the nobility; peasant enfranchisement −10%; nobles allowed to expand R.G.O.s; monthly progress +0.05 to land, +0.10 to aristocracy, +0.10 to serfdom; allows the noble villa (the game's tooltip)
data.concession: its slow unravelling in the integrated territories
data.compensation: a stipend for the nobility's arts and culture

source: Trent's account and screenshot of the Land Rights privilege, 8 April 1438
